findings.summary: The planned scan for `Vec<Invocation>` fields misses lists written with a full type path, which is common in `Records`, so a fourth unchained list can pass.
findings.evidence: The `Records` struct writes many field types with full paths: `Vec<athena_data::records::AudienceRating>` (l.252), `Vec<athena_data::records::Audit>` (l.256), `Vec<athena_data::records::WorkItem>` (l.245). A new `pub hestia_runs: Vec<athena_data::records::Invocation>` would not match the pattern `pub <ident>: Vec<Invocation>`. It would not raise the count above 3 either, so the test passes while the list is left out of `all_invocations`. The fixed `== 3` also fails a correctly chained fourth list for the wrong reason, so the name check adds nothing. Fix: Treat a field as an invocation list when its type contains the path segment `Invocation` before a closing `>`, whatever prefix comes before it (for example the regex `\bInvocation>`, or the last path segment of the generic argument). Replace `== 3` with `>= 3`, so the check cannot go silently empty and a new list is judged only by whether it is chained.

findings.evidence: HISTORY.txt shows 41539a7 ('Retry 20261111-122637-aawj: role-need measure over all run sources') and b670592 already touched store.rs, role_need.rs, system-facts.md, spec.toml, status_role_need.rs and shard-timings.txt. The assertions the plan cites (role_need.rs:347-371 and 471-477, status_role_need.rs:160-168) are in the base. The new source-scan test passes on the base, which already chains all three lists. The new exhaustive-match test fails on the base only because `MEASURED_ROLES` does not exist yet. Each fails-without line describes a future edit, not a run the verifier can check. Fix: State in the Approach and the CHANGELOG that the root-cause fix landed in 41539a7 and b670592 and that this job adds the class guards. Put the scan in a small function, for example `unchained_invocation_lists(struct_src, fn_src) -> Vec<String>`. Unit-test it on a synthetic struct with a fourth list, spelled with a full path and not chained, and assert the function reports it; that test is in the diff and shows the guard failing. Reword the criterion 7 demonstration so the verifier looks for these guard assertions in the diff and not for the old steward, audience and auditor assertions.

summary: I read the code and HISTORY.txt; I ran nothing. The plan reads the code correctly. The base commit already has the root-cause fix: commits 41539a7 and b670592 add `Records::all_invocations`, the doc comments, the system-facts entry, OLY-9-11, the known-active replay tests and the window filter. So this job's diff is only two standing guards and one CHANGELOG sentence. That is the right size, and preferring information over a refusal rule is sound. Two problems remain. First, the new `Records` field scan matches only the short type spelling `Vec<Invocation>`. Many fields in that struct use full paths (`Vec<athena_data::records::...>`), so a fourth list written that way would get past both the name check and the fixed count of 3. Second, the request asks for a test that fails without the change, and criterion 7 has the verifier look in the diff for assertions on the steward, audience and auditor. Those assertions are already in the base, so the diff will not contain them. The new tests' fails-without cases are only described as hypothetical future edits; nothing in the diff shows them failing. The `from_parts` coverage test also keeps its own hard-coded list of roles, so it can drift in the same way the plan fixes for role_need. These can be fixed within the plan, so the verdict is revise.
